label: Rust server sandboxes
description: Rust modding is server-side. This describes what a sandbox does to a dedicated server, and why it does nothing to a client.

notes: There is no client-side Rust modding, and this app will not invent one. EasyAntiCheat runs in the kernel and treats a modified game folder as what it is; the cost of being clever here is somebody's Steam account, not a failed install. Point a Rust sandbox at a DEDICATED SERVER folder.

Copying is the default and the two link strategies are offered only because a server operator staging plugins on the same volume has a real use for them. EAC does not run on the server, which is why they are available at all.
Oxide (uMod) or Carbon has to be installed into the server folder first. A plugin deployed with no loader underneath it is a .cs file nothing will ever compile.

Oxide writes each plugin's configuration into oxide/config on first load and never overwrites it afterwards. Removing a plugin from a sandbox does not remove its config, which is deliberate — it is the thing you spent an evening tuning.

presets.label: Oxide / uMod server
presets.description: The long-established plugin loader. Nearly every published Rust plugin targets it.

presets.label: Carbon server
presets.description: A newer loader that is API-compatible with most Oxide plugins.

options.label: World size
